description: On **June 18, 1815**, in a single rainy day in Belgium, Napoleon's empire collapsed. Waterloo closed the Hundred Days and opened a century of monarchical order in Europe.

hero.hook: One day of mud in Belgium, and the Empire fell for good.

blocks.text: On **June 18, 1815**, near the Belgian village of **Waterloo**, the fate of Europe was settled in the rain. **Napoleon** faced two enemies at once: the Briton **Arthur Wellesley**, Duke of **Wellington**, and the Prussian **Gebhard von Blücher**.
This was not just a defeat. It was the end of the First Empire. In one day, the man who had dominated Europe broke apart on mud, on mistakes, and on an alliance that finally held together.

After his abdication in **April 1814**, Napoleon was exiled to the island of **Elba**, off the coast of Italy. The victors redrew Europe at the [[Congress of Vienna]]. On **March 1, 1815**, he landed near Antibes. The **Hundred Days** had begun: the troops sent to stop him joined him instead. He took Paris back without bloodshed.

blocks.caption: The return from Elba: Napoleon seizes power again

blocks.text: Napoleon and Wellington had never met before Waterloo. The Belgian battlefield was their only face-to-face encounter.

Europe declared him an outlaw. His plan was to use the [[central position]]. The idea was simple. Place himself between Wellington and Blücher, then beat them one after the other before they could join forces.

On **June 16**, Napoleon beat the Prussians at **Ligny**, a Belgian village. The same day, [[Marshal Ney]], one of his bravest generals, held the British at **Quatre Bras**, a strategic crossroads. But Napoleon believed the Prussians were finished. He sent Marshal **Grouchy** after them with **33,000 men**.
Some historians blame the late start on the morning of June 18 on an attack of hemorrhoids that kept Napoleon from riding out on his usual reconnaissance.

On the **18th**, after a night of rain, he waited until **11:30 a.m.** for the ground to dry. He wanted to move his [[Grand Battery]], a massive concentration of cannon. The delay gave Blücher time to march toward the sound of the guns.

sections.title: Two days earlier: Ligny and Quatre Bras

blocks.text: The battle opened around two fortified farms, **Hougoumont** and **La Haie Sainte**. Ney's charges broke against the British infantry, which formed [[Square]], a rectangle several ranks deep with bayonets facing outward. Around **4:30 p.m.**, the Prussians appeared on the French right flank. Grouchy stayed too far away.

As a last resort, Napoleon sent in the **Imperial Guard**, his elite unit. For the first time, it fell back. The cry “The Guard is retreating!” set off panic. The retreat turned into a rout. Wellington and Blücher met at **La Belle Alliance**.

sections.title: The day that broke the Empire

blocks.text: Napoleon abdicated on **June 22, 1815**. Exiled to **Saint Helena**, a remote island in the South Atlantic, he died in **1821**. The Congress of Vienna imposed [[Legitimacy]]: royal dynasties were put back on their thrones. Russia, Austria, and Prussia policed the continent. This “Concert of Europe” kept a relative peace until **1914**.

blocks.text: **Waterloo** (**June 18, 1815**) finished Napoleon. The late attack, Grouchy's absence, and the meeting of Wellington with Blücher brought down the Empire and opened a century of monarchical order.
